I appreciate how Schema runs parallel to AZ, in that while AZ gets more awesome any time he features in content, Schema gets more creepy as heck any time it features in content.

Especially since the yandere-ness is intensifying. “Well I could just easily go live my new life without any real bother, but NO you rejected me so now I’m going to kill you and all your little friends.”

Meanwhile Muerto just gets more adorable and earnest any time he shows up. The bit with him protecting AZ with his ghost suit especially was like dawwwwwww that’s so sweet!

I wasn’t expecting an episode with Badass Plucky Hero Boys instead of Sad Robot Boys, but I’m here for it.

In the questions section, that Groundhog Day story was so amazingly horrible I was almost morbidly chuckling at how over the top mean it was. I hope they keep it as canon, some metaverse writer would definitely make that kind of story.

And gosh I am always here for adorable Tachyon/AZ BFF moments.

Amusingly while discussing Haka hugs, they accidentally said Aeon Girl isn’t a person. Pretty sure that wasn’t intended.

PS: Exactly 100 episodes to go!

PPS: a soulmate for DS&PS would probably not naturally exist, but I could see The Fervor crafting a perfect “lover” for both of them, which probably goes wrong since passion isn’t love (see the Star Sapphire Corps in Detective Comics comics, where they use the word ‘love’ and clearly don’t know what it actually means).

PPPS: not to Americasplain the mythology of Japan, but my understanding is that yokai really aren’t anything close to demons, they’re more like what various D&D editions might call “monstrosity”, “magical beast”, or “monstrous human”, perhaps best translated as “creature”. The Japanese equivalent to “demon” as best I understand it is “bakemono”, so I find it odd that term isn’t the one they used for the thing that became Akari and which Akari now occasionally becomes under duress. (Legend of the Five Rings mostly uses “Oni” for demon while “bakemono” is treated as “monster”, but this is pretty clearly wrong, since the original mythical Oni were pretty specifically described as these tiger skinned giants with horns that are either red or blue…I think their closest equivalent in a western myth-cycle might be the Scandinavian trolls, which are likewise very definitely physical and humanoid, though they lean a little more nature-spirity. I think demon should pretty much always imply being “not of this world” in addition to fearsome or malevolent or otherwise monstrous.)
